what_its_for: Rolapitant is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy (cancer treatment). It is used along with other anti-nausea medicines to help you feel better during and after your chemotherapy sessions.
how_to_take: Take rolapitant by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. You will usually take this medicine about 1 to 2 hours BEFORE your chemotherapy starts. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you to.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 180 mg tablet taken once, about 1 to 2 hours before each chemotherapy treatment. You do not take this medicine every day — only on chemotherapy days as directed by your doctor. Do not take more than one dose per chemotherapy cycle (at least 2 weeks between doses).
missed_dose: Since rolapitant is taken only before chemotherapy, it is important to take it on schedule. If you forget to take it before your chemotherapy appointment, call your doctor or nurse right away for instructions. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store rolapitant tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging. Keep this medicine away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking thioridazine (a medicine for mental health conditions) while using rolapitant, as this combination can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because rolapitant can interact with many drugs. Avoid taking medicines that your body breaks down in the liver without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; unusual weakness or tiredness; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Rolapitant starts working within about 1 to 2 hours of taking it. It is designed to help prevent nausea and vomiting that can happen right after chemotherapy AND the delayed nausea and vomiting that can occur 1 to 5 days after your treatment.
special_populations: Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, your doctor may need to monitor you more carefully or adjust your treatment plan. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if rolapitant is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Older adults: Older patients can generally take the same dose, but should be monitored for any side effects or drug interactions.
